agree.reason: The plain apology and candid bad news would ease some of the cold investor's irritation, but with no numeric target for the reminder product and fundraising put off to the next update, they have little reason to commit more support yet.

honest.reason: Every figure matches the brief and the runway math is correct, though the claim that reminders work 'no matter which scheduler a clinic uses' and that they give customers 'another reason to stay' go a little beyond the stated facts.

works_the_facts.reason: It works out about 11 months of runway and the near-halving of no-shows, but it never says the lost chain was about 13% of revenue, gives no month when cash runs out, and doesn't say how many $150 subscriptions would replace the lost $5,500 (about 37) or cover the burn.

right_comparison.reason: It admits revenue is flat and calls runway the main concern, but it never spells out the do-nothing path: flat revenue with cash running out around next autumn, and the latest point to start raising money.

qualification.reason: The only commitment, to report how standalone reminders are selling next quarter, has no target number, deadline, or stated consequence if sales disappoint.

objections.reason: It deals head-on with the missed updates and promises regular reports, but it doesn't meet a lead investor's real question about runway and the next round with a concrete plan or decision point.

fit.reason: It is a well-organized investor email of about 430 words, under the 500-word limit, with clear sections and specific requests for help.
